steps.body: A **vector** carries two facts at once: a **magnitude** (how much) and a **direction** (which way). In components, v = ⟨a, b⟩ means 'go a right and b up.' Unlike a plain number — a scalar — a vector points somewhere. Velocity, force, and displacement are all vectors.
An arrow has a size and a direction — and components carry both.

widget.prompt: u is the zero vector, so u + v is just v. Land the sum on (3, 4) and read the length.
widget.successFeedback: v = (3, 4), and its length is √(3² + 4²) = 5. The two components are not the vector — they are a recipe for reaching it: 3 across, then 4 up. Length and direction are what the arrow actually IS.
widget.lowFeedback: The horizontal part is wrong — the sum must land 3 to the right.
widget.highFeedback: The horizontal part is right but the height is wrong — the sum must land 4 up.

cml.actionGoal: Change vector components and coordinate geometric movement with component and dot-product representations.

predict.prompt: The vector ⟨3, 4⟩ has components 3 and 4. Its LENGTH will be…
predict.reveal: 5, by Pythagoras. The components are the two legs of a right triangle, not pieces to be totalled. Adding them measures a journey along the grid lines; the vector's length is the straight line cutting across.

explanationVariants: |⟨−3, 4⟩| = √((−3)² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = 5 — squaring erases the negative, so it matches ⟨3, 4⟩.
The length is the same 5; only the DIRECTION differs (this one points up-left).

widget.prompt: What is the magnitude of v = ⟨−3, 4⟩?

numericErrors.feedback: 1 = −3 + 4 adds signed components. Magnitude squares first: √(9 + 16) = 5.
A magnitude is a LENGTH, never negative: √((−3)² + 4²) = 5.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the required exact-number states before checking.

steps.body: Magnitude is pure Pythagoras: |⟨a, b⟩| = √(a² + b²). The components are the legs of a right triangle; the vector is the hypotenuse. That's why ⟨3, 4⟩, ⟨5, 12⟩, and ⟨6, 8⟩ have the clean lengths 5, 13, and 10 — they're the Pythagorean triples.

explanationVariants: A vector's magnitude follows a² + b² = c²; here 6² + y² = 10², so y = √(100 − 36) = 8.
Same 6-8-10 triple as before, solved for the missing leg instead of the hypotenuse.

widget.prompt: A vector v = ⟨6, y⟩ has magnitude 10. What is y (given y > 0)?

numericErrors.feedback: 4 = 10 − 6 subtracts directly. Magnitude uses squares: y = √(10² − 6²) = √64 = 8.
64 = 10² − 6² is under the root — take the square root: √64 = 8.

explanationVariants: Speed is a scalar (just a number); velocity is a vector (speed AND heading). The extra fact is direction.
A vector adds direction to a magnitude — that's the whole distinction.

widget.prompt: Which quantity is a VECTOR, not a scalar?

options.label: Velocity (50 km/h north)
options.feedback: Right — it has a magnitude AND a direction, the defining vector traits.

options.label: Temperature (20°C)
options.feedback: Temperature is a plain number — a scalar. Velocity, with its direction, is the vector.

options.label: Mass (5 kg)
options.feedback: Mass is a scalar. The vector here is velocity, which carries a direction.

explanationVariants: The drone's displacement is ⟨5, 12⟩ from the launch point, so its distance is √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 km.
Treat the two flight legs as vector components and apply the same magnitude formula: 13 km.
hints: The two flight legs ARE the vector's components: ⟨5, 12⟩.

widget.prompt: A drone launches, flies 5 km east, then 12 km north. Directly from the launch point, how far away is the drone now, in kilometers?

numericErrors.feedback: 17 = 5 + 12 adds the legs directly. The displacement is ⟨5, 12⟩, whose magnitude is √(25 + 144) = 13 km.

widget.fallbackFeedback: The flight legs are the vector's components ⟨5, 12⟩: √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 km.
widget.successFeedback: The flight legs are the vector's components ⟨5, 12⟩: √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 km.

takeaways: A vector ⟨a, b⟩ bundles magnitude and direction.
Magnitude = √(a² + b²), always ≥ 0 — the sign lives in the direction.
Vectors model directed quantities: velocity, force, displacement.

concept.body: Vector ⟨a, b⟩: magnitude √(a²+b²), a length that is never negative. The components are the legs of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is the vector.

explanationVariants: |⟨0, −5⟩| = √(0 + 25) = 5 — a purely vertical vector of length 5.

widget.prompt: What is the magnitude of v = ⟨0, −5⟩?
